title: Migrations and schema changes without stopping the system

videos.script: Adding a column takes two milliseconds. In this lesson it also stops every sale for eighteen seconds. {{alter}} The column needs a strong lock for an instant. A long transaction is holding a weak one, so the change waits, and every sale that arrives after it waits behind it. {{queue}} A lock timeout turns that wait into a quick failure you can retry. {{timeout}} Some changes rewrite the whole table while they hold the lock. You will tell them apart by the file they write. {{rewrite}} An index built the usual way stops sales for four seconds. Built concurrently, the box office never notices. {{index}} Then the safe way to make a change nobody can make at once: expand, backfill in small batches, and add the constraint without a long lock. {{expand}}
